checks.finding: REQ-001..REQ-007 each state concrete, measurable predicates (required key sets, three named regex patterns, minLength/minItems bounds, seven-item validator check list (a)-(i) with exit-code/1-line-per-violation output contract, byte-identical v1 non-modification). No requirement is stated only as intent; each maps to an observable validator behavior or a diffable artifact property (e.g. REQ-007's SHA-256 non-regression). No contradiction found across Goals/Non-goals/Edge Cases.

Positive-capability matrix row 'G1: optional フィールドは不在でも受理される | AC-004, AC-020 | optional 配列を持たない契約が exit 0 で通過する（AC-004 の Book/Bookshelf 正例と AC-020 末尾の不在 canary）' cites AC-004 as evidence that an optional field can be entirely absent, but AC-004's own Test Target reads: '同 suite: Book/Bookshelf 正例 fixture（Book.must_not_own に display position / Placement concept が並び責務）が通過' — i.e. Book.must_not_own is explicitly *populated* with 'display position' in that very fixture, the opposite of absent. AC-020's canary text ('あわせて、当該 optional 配列自体を持たない fixture（AC-004 の正例系）が exit 0 で通過することを示し...') is scoped to the two object-arrays discussed in AC-020's four preceding sub-fixtures (stakeholder_perspectives, distinguished_from — arrays whose elements have nested required sub-fields, which is what AC-020's own text is about); it does not name must_not_own, which is a plain string array with no nested required fields and therefore falls outside AC-020's stated scope. No AC in the table (AC-003, AC-004, AC-005, AC-013, AC-025) states a fixture where must_not_own is entirely omitted and the concept still passes. The row's own governing rule ('全称の記述を使う場合は...各要素が引用 AC の Test Target に名前で現れることを確認する') is therefore not honored for one of the three named optional fields. Downstream failure: REQ-005's fixture-corpus author, relying on this row as proof that the 'optional-absent' capability is already fixture-covered for all three optional fields (mirroring the immediately preceding 'optional 3 種の populate' row), could ship the corpus without ever exercising a must_not_own-entirely-absent-and-passing case — even though requirements.md's own Edge Cases section ('must_not_own が空/欠落: 有効（初期は責務だけ列挙し...）') requires this behavior. This is spec-review scope because it is exactly the matrix self-consistency audit this round's edit_summary claims to have completed (round-1's Major was the same class of overclaim on G1), and Major because it is a missing observable acceptance criterion for a stated capability, not a contradiction that makes the spec unreviewable.

Every AC (AC-001..AC-025) specifies a concrete, externally checkable outcome: exit code, stderr content (field name / expected type / violation message), or a byte/hash comparison. Bounded-quantifier ACs (AC-014 7 fixtures, AC-018 3, AC-019 3, AC-020 4, AC-021 7, AC-022 2, AC-023 8, AC-024 29) enumerate each element by name and each enumeration's count matches the corresponding Field Definitions / REQ-002 declaration (e.g. AC-014's 7 required fields = the 7 'Yes'-required rows in Field Definitions; AC-023's 8 minLength targets = the 8 items REQ-002 lists as minLength-1). No vague-intent criterion found.

Non-goals explicitly excludes concept-test skill/bootstrap, template/interviewer stage changes, reviewer A/B checks, reverse mode/C4, v1->v2 migration tooling, domain/ artifact generation, and mechanical enforcement of meta.status Approved — each with a phase pointer or explicit rationale (e.g. 'v1 → v2 の移行ツール・二重バージョンローダー（owner 決定により恒久的にスコープ外。INV-009）'). Roles and Permissions further states the approval boundary is human-only by explicit design, closing off an area that could otherwise silently expand into enforcement tooling.

Material constraints are explicit: byte-for-byte v1/consumer non-modification quantified via SHA-256 drift lock (REQ-007, AC-002), security/data constraints in 'Security Boundaries' (content-as-data, no network access, no external dependencies beyond python3 stdlib json / ConvertFrom-Json, no secrets in fixtures), and the approval-boundary gap is stated as a known, deliberate non-goal rather than left ambiguous ('meta.status の Approved 書込に対する機械的強制は存在しない...承認境界は人間のレビュー運用のみが担保する').

Risks R1-R3 each name a concrete future validation surface: R1 -> 'fixture corpus を先に書き、Phase 1 の判定4種が必要とするフィールドを受け入れテストで先取り検証する'; R2 -> 'REQ-006 のテストが schema ファイルの required/pattern 宣言と validator の挙動を同一 fixture で突き合わせる'; R3 -> 'REQ-006 の twin parity 検査（同一 fixture・同一 verdict）', which maps directly to AC-013. No high-risk claim is left without a stated mitigation path.
